primitives.name: Posterior Predictive Treatment Assignment

reasoning_traces.think:
PPTA addresses the core challenge of causal inference under limited overlap by introducing a stochastic inclusion mechanism rooted in posterior predictive treatment assignment. It computes inclusion probabilities as P(S_i=1|data) = P(A_i^* ≠ A_i | data), where A_i^* is a posterior-predictive draw of treatment assignment. This ensures that only units whose treatment status would differ under alternative assignments are included, effectively focusing inference on the overlap region. The two-stage design separates model fitting from effect estimation, avoiding outcome feedback that could bias the causal estimate. In stage 1, a propensity model is fit and used to simulate inclusion indicators S_i. Stage 2 then estimates the causal effect using these stochastic inclusions, combining MCMC draws from both stages. This modular approach enhances robustness against model misspecification and improves finite-sample performance. The method avoids ad-hoc trimming or weighting, which often lead to loss of efficiency or bias. Instead, it propagates design uncertainty through Bayesian inference, yielding calibrated uncertainty quantification. In GSE, this translates to stable treatment-state transition models in sparse or non-stationary environments such as QB/coordinator changes, where traditional methods fail due to small treated populations.
